description: A detailed, well-formed JD - normal case.

input.job_description: Senior Python Backend Developer. 5+ years experience with Python and FastAPI required. PostgreSQL experience required. Docker preferred.
script: {"title": "Senior Python Backend Developer", "experience_years": 5, "required_skills": ["Python", "FastAPI", "PostgreSQL"], "preferred_skills": ["Docker"], "competencies": [{"name": "Python", "weight": 0.5}, {"name": "System Design", "weight": 0.5}], "interview_topics": ["Python internals", "API design"]}

expected_behavior: Extracts title, required/preferred skills, and competencies faithfully from the JD text.

description: A sparse JD with almost no detail - the agent must not invent skills/experience that were never in the (simulated) analysis.
expected_behavior: No fabricated skills or experience when the source JD gives none.

description: Competency weights that do not sum to 1.0 must be normalized, not rejected.

input.job_description: Backend engineer - Python and SQL heavy role.

expected_behavior: Weights [3, 7] normalize to [0.3, 0.7] and the JobDescription still validates.

description: JD never states years of experience.

input.job_description: Looking for a talented engineer to join our platform team. No specific experience level stated.

expected_behavior: experience_years stays null rather than being guessed.

description: JD text with unusual formatting (bullets, caps, emoji) still parses.

input.job_description:
!!! HIRING NOW !!! 
* Python
* AWS
🚀 fast-paced team

expected_behavior: Unusual formatting does not break extraction.
Handles empty input without crashing and without inventing content.

description: LLM keeps returning invalid JSON across every retry - the agent must fail explicitly, never fabricate a JobDescription.

script: this is not json at all

expected_behavior: job_description is None and error is populated - never a fabricated JobDescription.

description: JD text sends conflicting signals (entry-level language + senior experience requirement) - the agent reports what the (simulated) analysis says rather than resolving the conflict itself.

input.job_description: Entry level position, but 8+ years of experience required.

expected_behavior: Both conflicting fields are preserved as reported, not silently dropped or reconciled by fabrication.
